lib.intro: Every snippet starts with `from elo_playground import connect` (or the Node / browser equivalent). That is this library - a small, heavily-commented wrapper around the raw IX REST calls, with the same surface in all three runtimes. It is NOT part of ELO; it lives in this project under shared/ and you can copy it into your own code.
lib.m.connect: Build a client from ELOPG_* environment variables (or the connection form) and log in. Returns a MockEloClient in mock mode.
lib.m.call: One IX RPC call: POST {base}/rest/IXServicePortIF/<method>, returns the result, raises EloError on the {exception} envelope.
lib.m.login: Open the IX session. connect() already does this for you.
lib.m.findall: Run a findFirst / findNext / findClose pagination loop to the end and return every row.
lib.m.blob: GET / POST a document's bytes on the same authenticated session (download URL from checkoutDoc, upload URL from checkinDocBegin).

labperm.modeDiagTitle: Scan the tree for ACL problems and explain each one
labperm.modeOrgTitle: Group nesting and the supervisor tree, drawn as a chart
labperm.diagNone: nothing to report - no finding in the scanned folders
labperm.diag.orphan_entry.title: ACL entry points to a deleted group/user
labperm.diag.orphan_entry.why: The entry names an id that no longer exists in the user directory. It grants nothing today, but it is noise that hides the real permissions, and if ELO ever reuses the id (or an import recreates it) the folder silently opens up to whoever gets that id.
labperm.diag.orphan_entry.fix: Open the folder's permissions in the ELO client (or run checkinSord with the cleaned aclItems) and remove the entry. If it was a group, check whether the folder still has a valid grant for the people who used it.
labperm.diag.admin_only.title: Only administrators can reach this folder
labperm.diag.admin_only.why: No non-administrator group, user or owner has any access bit here. Main administrators bypass the ACL, so from their client the folder looks normal - but every regular user gets 'no access'. Typically left behind after a group was removed or a project ended.
labperm.diag.admin_only.fix: Decide whether the folder is still needed. If yes, grant the right group (prefer groups over single users); if it is an archive nobody should touch, it is fine - just document it. Use 'By folder' on it to double-check who ends up with access.
labperm.diag.write_without_read.title: Write/Delete/Edit/Permission granted without Read
labperm.diag.write_without_read.why: The entry grants W, D, E or P but not R. ELO honours the bits literally: the principal may change or delete something they cannot open or even see listed - a trap for users and a classic sign of a mis-clicked checkbox. In 'By group / user' such folders show up as e.g. (W) alone.
labperm.diag.write_without_read.fix: Add Read (and usually List) to the entry, or remove the write bits if the principal should not touch the folder at all. The usual sane sets are R+L (see), R+W+L (work) and full (63) for owners of the area.
labperm.diag.everyone_full.title: An everyone-group gains full access here
labperm.diag.everyone_full.why: A group every single user belongs to (e.g. 'Jeder') gets all 63 bits on this folder although the parent did not grant that. Every user can therefore delete, move and re-permission everything below - the parent's more careful setup is undone from here down.
labperm.diag.everyone_full.fix: Reduce the everyone-group to R+L (or remove it) and grant the working rights to the specific team group instead. Check the children afterwards: ELO copied this ACL onto every folder created below it.
labperm.diag.empty_group.title: Granted group has no members
labperm.diag.empty_group.why: The entry grants access to a group nobody belongs to - not directly, not through a sub-group. Either the group was emptied when people left and the folder is now unreachable for the team, or it is a placeholder that was never filled.
labperm.diag.empty_group.fix: Add the intended members to the group (Admin Console > Users and groups), or replace the entry with the group that actually holds the team. Keep the group if it is a role placeholder you will fill later.
labperm.diag.and_unsatisfiable.title: AND-group entry no existing user satisfies
labperm.diag.and_unsatisfiable.why: The entry only applies to users who are in the group AND in every listed AND-group. Right now no user is in all of them, so the entry grants nothing - the folder may be unreachable for the people it was meant for.
labperm.diag.and_unsatisfiable.fix: Either add the intended users to the missing group(s), or drop the AND condition and grant the single group that describes them. Use 'By folder' to confirm someone finally resolves to access.
labperm.diag.users_without_groups.title: Users that belong to no group (besides everyone)
labperm.diag.users_without_groups.why: These users only reach folders through everyone-groups or through entries naming them personally. Per-user entries scatter across the tree, are forgotten when the person changes role and make 'who can see this' impossible to answer from the group model.
labperm.diag.users_without_groups.fix: Put each user into the group that matches their role (department / project) and grant folders to groups. Service or technical accounts are the exception - they are fine without groups.
labperm.diag.groups_without_members.why: Nobody belongs to these groups, directly or through nesting. Every ACL entry granting them is dead weight, and an administrator reading a folder's permissions is misled into thinking a team has access.
labperm.diag.groups_without_members.fix: Fill the group, or delete it and remove its ACL entries (the 'empty group' findings above list the folders). Keep deliberate role placeholders, but name them so (e.g. a 'Role-' prefix).
labperm.orgLegend: Groups: a group's own groupList names its parent groups, so a group is drawn under each parent (↗ = it has several). Click a group to see its direct members; [👤 n] = direct members. Dashed = an everyone-group (every user belongs to it). Supervisors: UserInfo.superiorId, the supervisor set in the user's profile; click a person to see their groups. ELO has no org-chart RPC - this is built from findFirstUsers + checkoutUsers.
